title: How container networking works on Linux
author: Julia Evans

body:
I spent last week figuring out how container networking actually works under the hood. It turns out it is all veth pairs and network namespaces. Here is what I learned by reading the kernel source.

When you run a container, the runtime creates a new network namespace using the clone syscall with CLONE_NEWNET. Then it creates a veth pair: one end stays in the host namespace and the other gets moved into the container namespace.

Here is how to see it:

```
ip link show type veth
ip netns exec container1 ip addr
```

The bridge device connects all the veth host ends together. Packets from the container traverse the veth pair, hit the bridge, and get routed normally from there. NAT via iptables handles outbound traffic.

References:
- man 7 network_namespaces
- https://lwn.net/Articles/580893/
